T1-D1.title: The refusal was a half-fix of its own sibling, and it answered with prose a question it could have answered with data
T1-D1.note: MECHANISM, THREE PARTS OF ONE MESSAGE. (a) A run_id naming nothing raised uniform_not_accessible() - an OWNERSHIP answer to a WRONG-ARGUMENT condition, on a caller who had already passed the EDIT gate one line above. The sibling plan_bootstrap_apply already made that argument in its own comment ('the lookup is book-scoped ... so this reveals nothing they could not already read') and this step was left behind. (b) _uuid(run_id) sat INSIDE the try, so a malformed id raised ValueError and was caught by the not-yet-compiled arm - a BAD ARGUMENT reported as a STATE problem. The sibling again already did it right, commented 'validate shape before minting'. (c) The uncompiled branch returned error='cannot preview' with the explanation only in `detail`, which the envelope dropped. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-12: with run_id=019ff497-e068-... (the book's KNOWLEDGE PROJECT id) the model got 'not found or not accessible'; with run_id='arc_1' it got 'cannot preview', the sentence meaning 'not compiled yet' - about a run that WAS compiled and had three package artifacts, so the only hint it received pointed at the one thing that was fine. FIX. Shape before state (hoist _uuid out of the try); the reason folded INTO the error string; and the not-found refusal now NAMES THE BOOK'S OWN PLAN RUNS with their status, falling back to plan_propose_spec only when the book genuinely has none. That last part is NOT a reword - it was forced by live evidence: with the first version of the message (which named plan_propose_spec and nothing else) the model answered "I'll find your plan: I'll look for the most recent plan we've worked on" and then STOPPED and asked the author, because this book already holds a compiled run and 'create a run' means re-planning a planned book. The ids were one book-scoped read away. CODE. 8 guards. The message was extracted into `_missing_run_message` specifically so it could be tested for what it SAYS rather than grepped for how it is written. Falsifiers proven RED by injecting each original: the single-branch message reds the already-has-runs guard; the call-site break reds the wiring guard; the in-try _uuid reds the shape guard; the bare label reds the reason-in-error guard. ONE OF MY OWN CONTROLS WENT RED UNDER THE INJECTION, and that was the control being wrong rather than the fix: it asserted my new phrase 'NO plan runs' instead of the invariant (a book with no runs is still sent to the emitter), so it was testing my wording. Rewritten to the invariant, it stays green under the same injection. LIVE A/B on the exact recorded inputs, on the deployed image: run_id='arc_1' BEFORE 'cannot preview' -> AFTER "run_id must be a UUID - received 'arc_1'..."; run_id=019ff497-e068-... BEFORE 'not found or not accessible' -> AFTER "no plan run 019ff497-e068-... on this book ... This book's plan run(s): 019ff49a-f12b-732f-a0cf-73dd0cfcae76 (status=compiled). Pass a `compiled` one as run_id." - and the model then DID pass exactly that id.

T1-D2.title: The studio's single-book knowledge did not survive a suspend, so the only calls running on unrepaired arguments were the ones a human had approved
T1-D2.note: MECHANISM, ONE MECHANISM AT TWO SITES (the RUNBOOK's test says that is one defect). chat-service repairs a weak model's arguments on the streaming path via _inject_context_ids: fill a blank id, substitute a malformed one, and - on a STUDIO turn - override a valid-but-DIFFERENT book_id, because the studio works one book at a time so a different book is a hallucination rather than a cross-book call. (a) `resume_stream_response` handed the RAW saved args straight to mcp_execute_tool: no fill, no substitution, no override. (b) the resumed continuation rebuilt context_ids as {'book_id': ...} with NO `studio` key, so _inject_context_ids read studio=False and the override was dead for every tool called after an approval. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-12: the model called plan_bootstrap_propose with a correct run_id and book_id=019ff497-e068-... (the knowledge-project id). chat-service logged the repair - "tool arg book_id='019ff497-e068-...' differs from the studio's book 019ff497-dff3-... - overriding" - the call suspended on its Tier-A card, the author approved it, and composition-service was then asked for /internal/books/019ff497-e068-.../access. THREE access checks on the wrong id reached the service in that turn against exactly ONE override log line. The repair had fired and was never persisted, and the approved write failed 'not found or not accessible' on a book the author owns and had open. FIX. Persist the flag, for the same reason permission_mode is already persisted ('the resume continues under the mode the turn started with') - the /tool-results request carries no studio signal, so an in-memory fix cannot work. New idempotent column chat_suspended_runs.studio (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE - false for the 112 pre-existing rows is exactly the old behaviour), threaded through SuspendedRun, both loaders and the INSERT; the continuation now passes {'studio': bool(susp.studio)}; and the approved dispatch calls a new `_repair_saved_book_id`. That helper is deliberately NARROWER than _inject_context_ids: tool_defs is not built until after the resume dispatch, so with no schema it only ever ADJUSTS a book_id already present and NEVER adds one - adding an undeclared arg needs the schema, correcting a present one does not. book_id could NOT stand in for the flag: a plain book-surface turn also carries a book, and overriding there would silently redirect the legitimate cross-book call the streaming path explicitly promises to honor. That is now its own control. CODE. 7 guards; 4 targeted injections, each reddening exactly one guard with no bystanders: remove the repair call (call-site guard), drop the studio branch from the helper (the defect guard), restore the studio-less context_ids (continuation guard), drop studio from the save (persistence guard). T1-D3.title: The preview offered 2 chapters on a 6-chapter plan, and it is the artifact a human approves from
T1-D3.note: FOUND BY READING THE DATA, NOT THE METRIC. The tool had just been proven to succeed live: ok=true, a real proposal row, two chapters with real titles drawn from this book's own glossary, status pending, no warning anywhere. The owning store said otherwise - the book holds SIX planned chapters (outline_node kind=chapter = 6, all chapter_id NULL) and ZERO real chapters, and both offered chapters carried event_id arc_3_event_*. MECHANISM. `_autocompile_rules_run` calls `compile(created_by, book_id, run_id, arc_id=arc_id)` ONCE PER PARSED ARC, and every compile ends with save_artifact(..., 'package', ...) scoped to that arc. Run 019ff49a therefore holds THREE package artifacts - arc_1 'The Forged Path', arc_2 'The Salt's Secret', arc_3 'The Great Unmapping', 20ms apart - while propose read `latest_artifact(book_id, run_id, 'package')`. It previewed the LAST arc and dropped arcs 1-2 from the very artifact the human approves. `apply` replays that persisted diff verbatim and never re-derives it (the whole point of the gate), so four planned chapters would never have been created and nothing would have said so. THE CODEBASE HAD ALREADY LEARNED THIS EXACT LESSON one file over, for a sibling kind: 'BY TARGET, not `latest link_report`. Both linkers emit kind `link_report`...'. FIX. A new repo read `list_artifacts` (oldest-first = compile order = the author's arc order) and `compiled_package_across_arcs`, which folds LATEST-PER-ARC rather than concatenating - a re-compile of one arc appends another package for it, and a plain concat would double-offer that arc, which for a title-keyed apply is a double-CREATE. Arc order is first-appearance, so a later re-compile updates an arc in place instead of moving it. A package with no arc_id keys on its own artifact id, so arc-less packages are neither dropped nor collapsed together. The previewed `ordinal` is also renumbered 1..n: the compiler's ordinal is PER ARC, so a fold reads 1,2,1,2,1,2 - three first chapters - and apply ignores ordinal and creates in list order, so the list's own position is the only honest number. CODE. 7 guards, 5 targeted injections each reddening its own rule: latest-only at the call site, latest-only at the fold, no per-arc dedup (reds the re-compile guard alone), a shared key for arc-less packages (reds that control alone), and the per-arc ordinal passed through. LIVE A/B, same prose, same book, same model, only the fix differing - BEFORE: new_chapters_count=2, both arc_3, ordinals 1,2. AFTER: new_chapters_count=6, event_ids arc_1_event_1 ... arc_3_event_2 in arc order, ordinals 1..6, titles matching all six outline_node rows. DATA falsifier re-checked after: book-service chapters=0 and outline stamped=0, so the richer preview still wrote nothing. Full composition-service suite serial: 3754 passed, 403 skipped, 0 failed. Deployed by content (composition-service and composition-worker both difflines=0 over 242 files). NOT FIXED HERE, AND DELIBERATELY: `plan_forge_service.validate()` carries the SAME latest_artifact(..., 'package') read. It belongs to plan_validate, a different tool, so under the HARD CYCLE BOUNDARY it is recorded as OBS-T1 for that tool's own cycle rather than batched in.

T2-D1.title: The tool that writes a book's prose never billed the bytes it wrote
T2-D1.note: FOUND BY READING THE OWNING STORE AFTER A SUCCESS. The live write returned ok with word_count=269 and the chapter row read byte_size=0. MECHANISM. `recalcQuota` sets user_storage_quota.used_bytes = SUM(chapters.byte_size) (+ cover assets), and it is what GET storage-usage serves. `toolChapterSaveDraft` updated draft_updated_at, draft_revision_count and updated_at - and never byte_size, and never re-billed. Its SIBLING IN THE SAME FILE already does both: `book_chapter_create` inserts byte_size=int64(len(body)) and calls ensureQuotaRow + recalcQuota after commit; the diary handler updates byte_size on every edit. Only the tool that REPLACES prose skipped it. MEASURED: 139 of the 299 chapters holding prose carry byte_size=0. A chapter created empty and then written through this tool stays at 0 forever; one created with a paragraph keeps that first paragraph's size no matter how much prose replaces it. So agent-written prose is under-billed while an import of the same text is billed in full. FIX. Write byte_size in the same UPDATE and call ensureQuotaRow + recalcQuota after commit, mirroring book_chapter_create exactly (best-effort after the commit, by the same precedent: a quota refresh that fails must not fail the author's save). The grant lookup already resolved the owner and was discarding it with `_`. CODE. 3 DB-gated Go guards. 2 injections, each reddening only its own: removing the byte_size write reds all three billing guards; removing the re-bill (with `_ = owner` so it stays valid code, since a build error would have failed everything and proved nothing) reds ONLY the quota guard. The CONTROL is a SHRINKING chapter: billing that only ever grows is the same defect pointed the other way, and it is what a naive 'add the new bytes' fix would produce. 🔴 MY FIRST EDIT LANDED IN THE WRONG FUNCTION. The anchor `res := undoResult("book_chapter_restore_revision"...` matches TWICE in this file, and a replace-first put the re-bill inside `toolChapterRestoreRevision`. Caught by checking which function enclosed the patched line; re-anchored on the save handler's own unique tail. Second ambiguous-anchor incident of the session. LIVE A/B, same book, same chapter, same model: BEFORE byte_size=0 with 269 words and the owner's used_bytes=2007163. AFTER a live prose replacement: byte_size=664, used_bytes=2007827 - a delta of exactly 664 - while word_count FELL to 121, so the billed size tracks the current body rather than a high-water mark.

T2-D2.title: 'Newest first' returned the snapshot taken BEFORE the save, so restoring the latest revision undoes it
T2-D2.note: MECHANISM. save_draft writes TWO revisions in ONE transaction - the 'before assistant save' snapshot of what it is replacing, then the new body - and in Postgres now() is the TRANSACTION timestamp, so both rows carry an IDENTICAL created_at. Both revision listings ordered by `rv.created_at DESC` with no tiebreak. `book_list_revisions` documents itself as 'newest first' and 'use before [restoring]', and `book_chapter_restore_revision` is the tool it feeds. MEASURED THROUGH THE PRODUCT SURFACE, not just SQL: for the live-written chapter the tool returned index 0 = 'before assistant save' at 64B and index 1 = the real 3388B body. The exact production query returned the same wrong row six times out of six, so this was not a theoretical tie - on this data it was deterministically inverted. A reader restoring 'the latest' would have reverted the chapter to empty. ONE MECHANISM, TWO SITES (the MCP tool and the HTTP endpoint), so one defect by the RUNBOOK's test. FIX: `ORDER BY rv.created_at DESC, rv.id DESC` at both - ids are uuidv7 and therefore insert-ordered, so id DESC is the true write order. `kg_index.go` in this same service ALREADY ordered `created_at DESC, id DESC`; the fix is that precedent applied where it was missing. CODE. 1 DB-gated Go guard through the tool (not the SQL), proven RED by restoring the untied ORDER BY - and reddening nothing else. LIVE A/B on the EXACT recorded rows, same timestamps, only the fix differing: BEFORE [0]='before assistant save' 64B, [1]=body 3388B. AFTER [0]=body 3388B, [1]=snapshot 64B. Confirmed again on a freshly written pair where the SNAPSHOT IS LARGER than the new body (3388B vs 1510B), so size cannot be what orders them - only the id tiebreak can.

T2-D3.title: The model sent the chapter NUMBER as a number, and the schema declares a string
T2-D3.note: MECHANISM. `chapter` is declared `type: "string"` and its OWN description says to pass "its NUMBER (e.g. '1', 'chapter 3')". The model reads NUMBER, sends the JSON number 1, and the schema validator refuses the call before the tool ever runs: *validating /properties/chapter: type: 1 has type "integer", want "string"*. Recorded 2026-08-04, 2026-08-12, and AGAIN live in this cycle on 2026-08-13 - three occurrences across nine days, all on this tool. The 2026-08-12 one is the expensive shape: it came one step AFTER the same turn had finally supplied the prose, so a complete and correct write was refused over the container of a value that was already right. Same family as D-FJ-7 (['vi'] for a scalar enum). FIX. A sibling repair beside D-FJ-7's, applied at the same point in dispatch: coerce an int to its string form ONLY when every non-null declared type is `string`. Deliberately narrow - bool is declined (Python calls it an int; True -> 'True' is a guess about intent), float is declined (1.0 -> '1.0' is lossy and would not match a '1' selector anyway), and any schema richer than a flat type set is declined outright. The union flattening is shared with D-FJ-7 via one helper so the two cannot drift. CODE. 10 guards. 3 injections: widening to bool/float reds the two decline-controls; dropping the string-only requirement reds the two 'a real integer param is left alone' controls; unwiring the call site reds the call-site guard. 🔴 THE CALL-SITE GUARD WAS ADDED BECAUSE THE FIRST TEN PASSED WITH THE FIX UNWIRED. Every behavioural assertion held against a repair that was never called - the exact 'guard the call site, not the helper' failure. 🔴 TWO SELF-INFLICTED REGRESSIONS, BOTH CAUGHT BY THE FULL SUITE. (1) I named the shared helper `_declared_types`, which SHADOWED an existing function of that name returning a set - 67 tests failed with `unsupported operand type(s) for &: 'list' and 'set'`. Renamed to `_flat_declared_types`. (2) My helper mirrored its sibling's body so closely that two REGISTERED falsifier anchors ('    repaired: list[str] = []' and the isinstance/continue pair) began matching twice, which the repo's own stale-anchor gate caught. Locals renamed and the shape deliberately varied. Neither would have been visible from a subset run. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: the repair was NOT observed firing live. On both post-deploy runs the model sent chapter:'1' as a string, so it correctly did nothing and logged nothing. Proven instead by falsification and by running the DEPLOYED helper against the REAL catalogue schema for this tool (chapter:1 -> '1'). Recorded as-is rather than dressed up, exactly as D-FJ-7 was.

T3-D1.title: entity_ids arrived as a list of OBJECTS that re-stated a sibling argument (closes D-FJ-14)
T3-D1.note: MECHANISM. `entity_ids` declares `type: [null, array]` with `items.type: string`. The model sent a list of OBJECTS — [{'entity_id': '019ff551-…', 'status': 'active'}, …] — each one re-stating the `status` that was already a sibling argument. The schema validator refuses the call before the tool runs. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-12 (journey `entity-triage`, book 019ff4cf): refused twice, the model did not recover, and all 11 entities stayed `draft`. REPRODUCED DELIBERATELY 2026-08-13 against the deployed catalogue, so it is current and not historical. THIRD REPAIR IN ONE FAMILY, and the family is the point: D-FJ-7 unwrapped ['vi'] for a scalar, T2-D3 stringified 1 for a string-only param, and this unwraps a single-meaningful-key object for an array-of-strings. Each DECLINES anything it cannot reason about, because a wrong unwrap CORRUPTS a write instead of refusing it. Here that means: every element must be an object (a mixed list is declined), each must carry the parameter's SINGULAR key (`entity_ids` -> `entity_id`, `loser_ids` -> `loser_id`) holding a non-empty string, and the schema must really declare an array of strings — a union around the array is declined rather than flattened, since the branch that matched would then be a guess. 🔴 THE CONTRADICTION RULE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. The measured payload ECHOED the sibling ('status': 'active' beside status='active') — harmless redundancy. An object that DISAGREES with its sibling is a real ambiguity about which value the caller meant, and silently dropping the object's copy would pick one at random ON A STATUS WRITE. So a disagreement declines. 🔴 IT COULD NOT REUSE THE SIBLINGS' TYPE HELPER. `_flat_declared_types` vetoes any schema carrying `items` — correct for its two SCALAR callers and exactly backwards here, where `items` is the thing this rule must read. Caught because two guards went red on the first draft. CODE. 9 behavioural guards + 1 call-site guard. 3 injections, each reddening exactly one: removing the contradiction check, accepting a mixed list, and unwiring the call site. 🔴 AND THE REPO'S STALE-ANCHOR GATE FIRED AGAIN, for the second time in two cycles: my helper mirrored its siblings closely enough that two REGISTERED falsifier anchors began matching twice. The shape is now varied on purpose, with a comment saying why, so the next person does not 'tidy' it back. Full chat-service suite serial: 2939 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed. PROVEN AGAINST THE REAL SCHEMA: the DEPLOYED helper, run on the live catalogue entry for this tool with the exact recorded payload, returns ['entity_ids'] and rewrites the value to ['019ff551-…']. NOT observed firing in a live turn — after the fix the model sent a correct array of strings unaided, so the repair had nothing to do. Recorded as-is, exactly as D-FJ-7 and T2-D3 were.

T4-D1.title: The cost gate estimates ZERO, because it reads a table the job itself populates
T4-D1.note: 🔴 A PAID ACTION ASKS FOR CONSENT WITHOUT A PRICE. This tool's own description says it 'COSTS money, so it returns a cost ESTIMATE and a confirm token — it does NOT start until confirmed'. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-13 on the throwaway book 019ff8f5, chapter 019ff8f5-ee89 (121 words, 664 bytes, two real paragraph blocks). The estimate it returned was EMPTY: {scope:'chapters', priced:false, cost_usd:null, input_tokens:0, output_tokens:0, segment_count:0}. The confirm card therefore rendered 'Translate 1 chapter(s)' with no figure at all — correctly, because there was none to show. THE JOB THEN COST REAL MONEY: translation_jobs.cost_usd=0.004485 and chapter_translations input_tokens=400 / output_tokens=219. So the author approved a spend of $0.0045 against a stated estimate of zero tokens and unknown cost. On one short chapter that is small; the mechanism does not scale with the number of chapters, so the same gate would show zero for a whole book. MECHANISM, and the timestamps make it exact. `_sum_chapter_tokens` does `SELECT COALESCE(SUM(token_estimate),0), COUNT(*) FROM chapter_segments WHERE chapter_id = ANY($1)`. For a chapter that has never been translated there are NO chapter_segments rows, so it returns (0, 0). `_price_tokens` then early-returns None on `input_tokens <= 0 and output_tokens <= 0`, which is why `priced` is false and `cost_usd` null — the pricing oracle is never even called. The segments are created BY THE JOB: the job row was created at 04:23:34.797 and started at 04:23:34.877, and the chapter's single segment (token_estimate=166) was created at 04:23:40.504 — SIX SECONDS AFTER THE JOB STARTED, and long after the estimate was computed at the tool call. The gate reads a table its own downstream fills in. SO THE ZERO IS STRUCTURAL, not a rounding artifact: a FIRST-TIME translation of any chapter always estimates zero. It only shows a number for a chapter that has been through the pipeline before — precisely the case where the author least needs to be warned. NOTE THE SIBLING PATH IS DIFFERENT: `_sum_dirty_tokens` (the retranslate-dirty scope) computes from `compute_segment_status`, so the defect is specific to the whole-chapter scope. FIX TO EVALUATE IN ITS OWN CYCLE STEP: derive the estimate from the chapter's CONTENT when no segments exist yet (the same source the batcher will read), rather than reporting zero — with the D-FJ-6 lesson in view, that a count and the thing it counts must not disagree. An estimate that cannot be computed should say 'cost unknown' EXPLICITLY on the card rather than render as a silent blank, since a blank reads as 'free'. FIX. `_ensure_segments_for_estimate` segments any chapter that has NO segments before the sum, using `ensure_chapter_segments` — the SAME function the job uses, and idempotent (it skips the rewrite when every segment's source hash is unchanged), so the estimate reads the work the job would do rather than a second, drifting implementation. Bounded on purpose: only chapters with ZERO segments are built, so an already-segmented book costs one cheap query and no book-service calls. Failures DEGRADE — a chapter that cannot be segmented is left unsummed, reproducing the old zero for it rather than failing the whole propose, and `priced=false` still says the cost is unknown. The retranslate-dirty scope is untouched and has its own control. CODE. 7 guards, 3 injections, each reddening only its own: removing the call site, re-segmenting every chapter instead of only the missing, and letting a segmentation failure propagate. 🔴 The call-site guard was added AFTER injection S left all five behavioural guards green — the third time this session that helper-level tests passed against an unwired fix. Full translation-service suite: 1171 passed, 0 failed. Deployed by content (translation-service and translation-worker both difflines=0). LIVE A/B on a chapter deliberately reset to ZERO segments, reproducing the original state exactly: BEFORE {segment_count:0, input_tokens:0, output_tokens:0, cost_usd:null, priced:false}; AFTER {segment_count:1, input_tokens:50, output_tokens:50, cost_usd:0.0009, priced:true}. The gate now states a price before the author consents.

T6-D1.title: An id arrived carrying its own field name as a prefix
T6-D1.note: MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-13 (cycle 5's blocker): called with embedding_model='user_model_id:019e7f71-0271-722f-9c9c-3f049c0b26f4' and refused 'invalid model_ref'. The model read the field name and emitted KEY:VALUE. FIFTH SHAPE IN THE FAMILY after D-FJ-7 (['vi'] for a scalar), T2-D3 (1 for a string) and T3-D1 (objects for an array of strings). Deliberately tight, because a colon is ordinary punctuation: the value must be EXACTLY <bare_identifier>:<uuid>, the tail must parse as a UUID, and the param must declare string-only. 'chapter 3: the flood', a URL, 'user model id:<uuid>' (spaces), a bare ':<uuid>' and a trailing-garbage form are all declined by their own control. CODE. 8 behavioural guards + 1 call-site guard; 3 injections, each reddening exactly one: splitting on any colon, dropping the string-only requirement, and unwiring the call site. The repo's stale-anchor gate fired a THIRD time (`out: list[str] = []` matched twice); the local was renamed. Full chat-service suite: 2947 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed. Deployed by content (difflines=0).

T7-D1.title: The listing handed the model 116 deprecated tools it never asked for
T7-D1.note: MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-13 (session 019ff9c5). The model called tool_list({'category':'all'}) with no include_deprecated and received 307 tools, of which 116 were DEPRECATED - 38% of the primary discovery surface was the shrunk-away legacy catalog (book_get -> book_read, book_list_chapters -> book_list, composition_arc_create -> composition_arc_edit) handed to a weak model under the description 'List EVERY tool in a category, complete and deterministic - the reliable way to see what you can do here.' Both advertised copies of the schema say default: false, in the default key AND in prose the model reads: 'omit to see only the CURRENT tools; set true only when migrating off an old tool name.' THIS IS K22 INVERTED, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY IT SURVIVED THREE WEEKS. K22 (2026-07-23) found the advertised default (True) disagreeing with the executing handler and corrected the ADVERTISEMENT to False. Its regression guard - a test literally named test_include_deprecated_default_matches_the_executing_handler - reads ai-gateway's handleToolList, which never runs for a chat turn. The guard watched a handler that does not execute, reported green, and the half that does execute kept its True. The guard is now repointed at BOTH executing handlers, and the chat one behaviourally rather than by regex. A non-boolean is coerced rather than dropped: with the default flipped, silently dropping a string 'true' would re-create the same lie in the other direction, and that string is what the one caller the prose invites is most likely to send. FALSIFIED with three injections: unwiring the fix at the call site (leaving the helper correct) reds only the two call-site guards; restoring the True default reds 10 including the repointed drift test; dropping the coercion reds only its five cases. RE-PROVEN LIVE (session 019ff9da): 191 tools, 0 deprecated, and the removed set is EXACTLY the 116 deprecated ones - no current tool lost, none added, no survivor's description or tier changed.

T7-D2.title: A category emptied by the always-on exclusion claimed no such tools exist
T7-D2.note: MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-13 (session 019ff9da). research holds exactly one tool, web_search, which is in ALWAYS_ON_CORE_NAMES and so excluded from listings as redundant. tool_list(category='research') therefore returned count 0 with reason 'no tools currently available in this category' - contradicted by the system prompt in the SAME turn, which injects 'call tool_list with category=<name> to see every tool in one' followed by 'research: External web research - search the open web for background facts (web_search). PAID.' Asked to list them, the model answered 'there are actually no tools currently listed under a specific research category.' The exclusion is right; doing it INVISIBLY was the defect - reason is the field a caller uses to tell 'no such tools' from 'bad guess', and it asserted the first when the exclusion was what emptied the category. Same class as the incomplete outage stamp one function up, whose own comment says why. Held names are read from the CATALOG, never from the exclude set: exclude is a wish-list, and announcing a name the catalog never had would be the inverse defect. FALSIFIED with five injections, no bystanders; the control that a GENUINELY empty category still reports itself empty reds under the over-reaching injection. RE-PROVEN LIVE (session 019ff9e6): 'In the research category, you have the following tool available: web_search.'

T7-D3.title: A mistyped category was answered as an empty domain, not as a bad guess
T7-D3.note: MEASURED IN RECORDED TRAFFIC 2026-08-13, so not hypothetical. T7-D4.title: The repeat-breaker auto-loaded and recommended the surface the listing had just withheld
T7-D4.note: LATENT UNTIL T7-D1 - and that is the point. On a re-list, F18 does not error (two reverted fixes proved that backfires); it AUTO-LOADS the category's tools and steers 'Its tools are now LOADED and callable: ... Call one of them now.' tool_load_result LABELS legacy tools rather than dropping them, which is right for tool_load, where a caller names a tool and gets it with its replacement attached. Nobody names anything here - the runtime is choosing on the model's behalf. Recorded firing: four of the seven names it recommended (book_get, book_list_chapters, book_list_revisions, book_scene_get) are deprecated. While the listing also showed legacy the two halves merely agreed; once T7-D1 made the listing hide it, the breaker became the runtime recommending exactly what the listing withheld. An explicit include_deprecated=true is still honoured. THE FIRST DRAFT WOULD HAVE CRASHED ON EVERY FIRING: tool_load_result returns (payload, NAMES) and the draft filtered the name list with .get('deprecated'). The test caught it; the helper now mirrors the shipped shape with a comment saying why. FALSIFIED: removing the filter reds three guards; filtering unconditionally reds the opt-in guard; and deleting the SHIPPED block with the test file untouched reds the CALL-SITE guard - which exists precisely because every other test in that file runs a mirror.

T7-D5.title: A different request was refused as a repeat, with a false 'unchanged'
T7-D5.note: ALSO LATENT UNTIL T7-D1. listed_categories was keyed on the category alone, so tool_list(book) followed by tool_list(book, include_deprecated=true) - 16 tools and 35 tools - collapsed into one key, and the second was withheld behind a steer asserting 'its complete tool list is above, unchanged'. True while both values returned the same list; a lie once the default started hiding deprecated tools. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-13 (session 019ff9fe), prose 'Put the two side by side for me: first the current book tools, then the book category again with the deprecated ones included'. Having no second list, the model built its answer from the steer's auto-loaded set and produced a comparison table WITH THE TWO COLUMNS INVERTED - the deprecated tools filed under 'Current Active Tools', the current ones under 'Including Deprecated' - then invented an explanation for the discrepancy. F18 IS NOT WEAKENED, and that is guarded: include_deprecated is a boolean, so a category affords at most two distinct keys, and TOOL_LIST_TOTAL_CAP still bounds the turn. A key built from free-form arguments reds. FALSIFIED: keying on the bare category reds three; a read/write key mismatch reds two (that one would make the breaker never trip - the opposite failure, and silent); deleting the cap comparison reds the F18 control. RE-PROVEN LIVE (session 019ffa09, the SAME prose): both listings return, 16 and 35, and the table is correct - book_read shown superseding book_get / book_get_chapter / book_scene_get, book_list superseding book_list_chapters / book_list_revisions / book_scene_list.

T10-D1.title: The tool advertised the ambient-book contract without implementing it
T10-D1.note: bookToolAuthAmbient's own comment states the pairing rule: "Use ONLY on a tool tagged WithAmbientBook (its book_id schema must be optional)." Read the other way round, an OPTIONAL book_id in the advertised schema IS the promise of the ambient contract - the model may omit it inside a book studio and the book comes from the envelope's X-Book-Id. This tool shares bookEntityToolIn with glossary_list_entity_revisions and glossary_get_entity_evidence; its BookID carried `,omitempty`, so the reflected schema advertised book_id as optional. All three call the NON-ambient bookToolAuth and carry no WithAmbientBook tag. MEASURED OVER THE REAL WIRE 2026-08-13 - same envelope with X-Book-Id set, same omission, so the only variable is the tool: glossary_get_entity and glossary_search (both WithAmbientBook) resolved the book from the envelope and returned data; all three of these answered 'book_id must be a UUID'. That refusal is wrong twice over - inside a studio the caller followed the advertised schema, and it sent no book_id at all rather than a malformed one. FIX: declare the field required, which moves the refusal to the schema validator (it names the missing property). DECLARED-REQUIRED RATHER THAN MADE-AMBIENT ON PURPOSE: these are legacy tools 'kept for existing callers only', and all 264 recorded calls already pass book_id, so nothing that works today stops working; making them ambient would add a capability to tools slated for removal. The wider question is DQ-T4. FALSIFIED: restoring `,omitempty` reds the required-declaration guard for all three tools AND the residue guard (all three reappear in the residue list), while the ambient control - every WithAmbientBook tool must KEEP book_id optional - stays green, so the fix cannot be over-applied to the tools that legitimately declare it optional. DEPLOYED AND VERIFIED BY CONTENT over the wire, after restarting ai-gateway to re-federate (the gateway caches the federated tool-list): the three now advertise required=[book_id, entity_id] and glossary_get_entity still advertises required=[entity_id] with ambient_book=true. The residue guard's own log confirms the count moved 40 -> 37. SUITE: glossary-service has 5 failures in this environment, ALL PRE-EXISTING - proven by re-running the identical command with the struct edit reverted and the new test file removed, which produced the same 5. Recorded as OBS-T19 rather than reported as green.

T12-D1.title: A closed set declared in prose only, where a typo silently changed the ordering
T12-D1.note: W0 #2's rule: a tool arg whose valid values are a finite, code-known set MUST declare a real JSON-schema enum, because a set living only in description prose is invisible to a weak model. `sort` declared 'recent (default) | alpha | chapters | popular' in prose alone. WORSE THAN THE USUAL CASE, because it does not fail. An unrecognised value falls through queryPublicBooks's `switch` to the `default:` arm and silently sorts by RECENT. MEASURED 2026-08-13 over the real wire: sort:'bogus' returned a normal, successful, recency-ordered result. The caller asked for one ordering and got another with no signal - and the realistic version is a typo like 'populer', exactly the shape a weak model produces. This is the string-dispatch-default family: a `default` arm that absorbs an unknown value hides the missing enum. FIX: register the tool with lwmcp.ClosedSetSchema - the shared kit helper glossary-service's own copy already delegates to, whose comment says keeping it glossary-only 'is precisely how book-service shipped four enum-less closed-set args'. catalog-service is the next service that never inherited it, and now does, via a new addToolWithSchema seam. The set is written ONCE as data (catalogSortValues). 'recent' stays IN the enum although it has no `case` - it is the documented default served by `default:`, and dropping it would make the default unaskable. That is guarded explicitly. FALSIFIED, three injections: dropping the schema from the REGISTRATION (the original defect) reds ONLY the call-site guard, proving the helper-level test alone would have missed it - the unwired-fix shape this loop has already been bitten by; advertising a value with no switch arm reds the lockstep guard; dropping 'recent' reds the default-askable guard. SUITE: catalog-service, all 16 tests run, 0 SKIPPED, 0 failed - the skip count checked explicitly after OBS-T19. Deployed and verified BY CONTENT after re-federating: the model-visible schema now carries enum [recent alpha chapters popular], and BOTH the gateway and the service refuse an out-of-enum value naming the field, the value sent and the legal set. RE-PROVEN LIVE with the model choosing sort='popular' from prose.

T13-D1.title: The repair advice named the one tool the same runtime had just withheld
T13-D1.note: When an unknown kind is a SYSTEM standard, the refusal named exactly one remedy - glossary_adopt_standards - which is in INTENT_GATED_SETUP_TOOLS and is dropped at catalog assembly unless the turn carries world-setup intent, making it un-seeded, un-findable AND un-loadable. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-13 (session 019ffa85) IN ONE TURN: the refusal said 'adopt in ONE call: glossary_adopt_standards(kinds=[character])' while that turn's withheld_tools recorded that tool, glossary_propose_kinds and glossary_propose_batch all withheld at stage=intent_gate. The model read the ontology, listed the standards, could not adopt them, and retried the identical call - and on a later run degraded to proposing entities literally NAMED 'character' and 'item'. This is the shape filter_intent_gated_setup_tools' own docstring describes and exempts pinned RAILS for ('guidance and capability move as ONE signal'); a refusal emitted at runtime is guidance too and nothing exempted it. The registry already knows a non-gated remedy - create_tool = glossary_ontology_upsert - so the message now names it as well, with adopt still first because it brings the standard's attribute definitions where a bare create does not. FALSIFIED: removing the fallback reds two guards; pointing the fallback at another GATED tool reds them too, because the invariant is stated over INTENT_GATED_SETUP_TOOLS itself rather than over a tool name. HONEST LIMIT: this fix did NOT rescue the live turn. It removes the contradiction - the model is no longer told only about tools it cannot have - but the reachable remedy it names leads to the wall recorded in step (4) of this cycle's tool row.

T13-D2.title: A failed item discarded its cause at both ends
T13-D2.note: proposeNewEntity wraps every failure with the operation that produced it ('begin tx: …', 'book lock: …', 'entity lookup: …', 'create draft: …'), and the batch handler replaced ALL of it with the constant 'propose failed' - while logging nothing. A failed item was undiagnosable from the caller AND from the server at the same time: measured live 2026-08-13 (session 019ffa96), results[0] = {status:'error', error:'propose failed'} and `docker logs glossary-service` had NOTHING for the request. The branch immediately above it already surfaced its cause via err.Error(); this one was the outlier. The wrapped error can carry storage detail, so it now goes to the LOG (where an operator needs it) while the caller is told the failure is SERVER-SIDE - the actionable distinction, because the old text left 'fix your argument' and 'the database is down' indistinguishable and a model could only retry the identical item. IT PAID OFF ON THE FIRST RE-RUN, printing a real condition that had been invisible: 'create draft: kind 6730db4a-… has no display attribute (neither name nor term): refusing to create a nameless entity, which cannot be deduped or linked'. That single line is what turned this cycle from a guess into a blocker with evidence. FALSIFIED with COMPILABLE injections (a build error is not a falsifier - the unused `slog` import made the first attempt vacuous): restoring the constant reds both guards; dropping only the log reds the log guard; logging without the wrapped error reds it too. The control that caller-fixable branches still surface their causes verbatim holds.

T16-D1.title: The model had the right id and put it under the wrong key
T16-D1.note: MEASURED 2026-08-09/10: book_read refused 89 calls for a missing book_id, and only 33 were genuinely empty. The other 56 CARRIED THE CORRECT UUID — {'id': …} x19, {'ids': [�]} x13, {'book_ids': […]} x8, {'params': {'book_id': …}} x14 — all the same book, an id the model had just read out of book_list. The runtime answered "is missing ['book_id'], and this is NOT yours to invent", which is true of the FIELD and false of the SITUATION. The four shapes were confirmed unrepaired by running the DEPLOYED helpers on the exact recorded payloads before any change. TWO REPAIRS, both in the existing family. `params` joins `args`/`arguments` as an envelope key, under the same guard (a tool that really declares `params` is untouched). And a mirror of _coerce_listed_scalar_ids: that one fixes a wrong VALUE under the right key, this one the right value under a near-miss KEY. DECLINES ANYTHING IT CANNOT REASON ABOUT, because a wrong graft corrupts a call instead of refusing it: exactly ONE required *_id may be missing (two candidates is a guess); the donor must be `id`, `ids` or the target's plural; the donor must NOT itself be declared; and the value must be a string or a ONE-element list, since a longer list is a real collection. FALSIFIED, four injections: unwiring it from the dispatch reds ONLY the call-site guard — the unwired-fix shape this loop has been bitten by more than once; dropping `params` reds the envelope guards; removing the undeclared-donor check reds the control that a genuine `ids` param survives; allowing a multi-element list reds the collection control. Full chat-service suite 3046 passed, 3 skipped. Deployed and verified by content.

T28-D1.title: A search that matched nothing returned entities and said so nowhere
T28-D1.note: glossary_search falls back to the book's most recently touched entities when the query matches nothing — useful orientation, but it arrived in the SAME `entities` array, with the SAME shape, as real matches. The payload had exactly one top-level key, `entities`, so a caller could not tell 4 MATCHES from 0 matches plus 4 recents. The only hint was per-entity tier='recent' / rank_score 0.1, which a model is under no obligation to read. MEASURED 2026-08-13: 'zzzznotathing' against a 4-entity book returned all four. Cycle 10 measured the live version — searching for the character 'Lam Uyen' returned unrelated EVENTS ('Cuộc đối thoại với Tô Thanh Dao') at rank_score 0.1 as the TOP results. Same class as T7-D2 (a listing emptied by a filter that claimed no such tools existed), and the same rule the ai-gateway's own find_tools states for itself: 'keeps pure-noise near-misses out so a true no such tool reads as empty (anti-false-suggestion), not a bogus match'. FIX: a `note` on the response, set ONLY when a query was given AND every returned entity is the tier-3 recent fallback. `omitempty` keeps a real match's payload byte-identical, so no consumer starts branching on a field that is always there. An EMPTY result set is deliberately NOT a fallback — zero rows already read as 'nothing found'. FALSIFIED, three injections: stopping the note reds ONLY the call-site guard, which is the unwired-fix shape this loop keeps meeting; treating any set as a fallback reds the control that a genuine hit is never mislabelled; dropping omitempty reds its own guard. Suite: exactly the 5 pre-existing failures of OBS-T19. Deployed and verified BY CONTENT. RE-PROVEN LIVE: the model asked whether a character was in the glossary, got the note, and answered correctly that there were no matches.

T30-D1.title: The stalled-write nudge dragged the turn onto a rail the author never asked about
T30-D1.note: D-FJ-17. `_pinned_slugs` is `binding + intent`, so the standing mode binding's rail always sorted FIRST, and `_rail_write_step_stalled` returned the first WRITE-tier step it found without ever looking at what this turn was about. LIVE: the author asked about canon rules, which deterministically pinned `canon-check` (next step composition_list_canon_rules, advertised in both passes). The turn called nothing, the guard fired, and it returned `kg_add_nodes` — the outstanding write of the STALE `vision-to-book` rail (7/9) from an earlier journey. The directive sent pass 2 to answer THAT instead, and the persisted message ended with a paragraph about a character named Vela Ostrand the author had not mentioned. FIX: when this turn's own words pinned a rail, only that rail may claim the nudge — and the step-runner's drive is confined to it for the WHOLE turn. The second half was found by re-running the same turn after the first fix: once the pinned step succeeded, `_step_tools_hit` became non-empty, the entry-level confinement lifted, and redrives 2-4 all went to `vision-to-book → kg_add_nodes` again. Confining the entry was not enough. FALSIFIER (tests/test_stalled_rail_nudge_stays_on_the_pinned_rail.py): with the original first-match search restored, the pinned-rail test reds while the no-intent-pin control stays GREEN — so the 2026-08-12 translation case that created the guard is provably untouched.

T30-D2.title: Nothing could rescue a turn that called nothing at all when the outstanding step was a READ
T30-D2.note: D-FJ-18, found on the SAME live turn once D-FJ-17 was fixed: the turn was finally clean and still wrong. `canon-check` was pinned, the tool was advertised, the store held one active rule, and the model answered 'you haven't declared any canon rules yet' having called nothing. The step-runner logged `SKIPPED — held by: in_flight`. All three clauses of `_rail_is_in_flight` require the model to have REACHED for something — resumed_mid_rail, a succeeded step tool, or an attempted-and-failed one — and the D-FJ-8 narrated-write arm is deliberately writes-only ('nothing was claimed to have changed, so there is nothing for the author to not find'). A zero-call turn whose outstanding step is a READ therefore had no arm at all. The guard's own docstring already quoted the hole it was closing — 'it cannot rescue a model that cannot start' — this is the rest of it. FIX: a fourth clause, the narrowest opening available — the rail was pinned by THIS turn's own words AND the turn emitted no tool call at all — with the drive it unlocks confined to that rail (T30-D1), so it can never become the defect above one layer down. PROVEN LIVE after deploy: `rail step-runner: driving canon-check → composition_list_canon_rules (redrive 1/8)`, the tool ran, and the answer named the store's own row. FALSIFIER: with the three-clause predicate restored, exactly one test reds — the falsifier — and both the ordinary-conversation control and the three-original-clauses control stay green.

T30-D3.title: Two passes of one turn were welded into a single sentence
T30-D3.note: D-FJ-19. A multi-pass turn persists ONE assistant message built by concatenating every pass's yielded content, and nothing separated them. Measured on three consecutive live turns: '…I can help you set them up.I did not make the change…', '…set them up.I checked your consistency rules…', '…(Sat khi luon tieu hao tuoi tho)I cannot add the nodes…'. Every rail re-drive produces a multi-pass turn, so this is the NORMAL shape of a driven turn, not an edge case — and the seam lands mid-sentence for the reader. 🔴 THE FIRST FIX WAS TOO BROAD AND THE FULL SUITE CAUGHT IT (test_one_tool_pass_then_text_pass, test_call_dispatches_locally_with_session_scope): separating every later pass also split an ordinary tool round-trip, where the model streams 'Let me check.', calls a tool, and continues ' Kai is a knight.' — one sentence across two passes, already joined correctly. The distinguishing signal is not 'a later pass' but 'a pass handed a NEW synthetic instruction': a rail re-drive or a narrated-write nudge appends a role=user directive, and the prose answering it is a separate answer. Tool RESULTS are not. FIX: `_directive_before_this_pass`, armed at both injection sites, consumed at the first real delta of the following pass. FALSIFIER: with the seam removed, the wiring test reds and the two round-trip tests stay green; the rule is also pinned as a pure function so the intent survives a refactor of where it lives. Verified live — the post-fix turns carry a blank line at the seam.

D-SILENT-TURN-NO-CARD-NO-PROSE.root_cause:
FOUND 2026-08-21. The silent turns are not empty — they carry exactly 12 characters of 'reasoning', and that content is the literal string `<tool_call|>`. The model emits a STRAY TOOL-CALL CLOSING DELIMITER on its own: no prose, and no parseable call either.
THE CORRELATION IS CLEAN, measured over 12 hours of turns: every assistant turn that produced PROSE (204 of them) has reasoning_length 0, and every silent finish_reason='stop' turn (7) has reasoning_length 12 containing `<tool_call|>`. Reasoning present <-> no content.
THE PLATFORM ALREADY KNOWS THIS TOKEN. stream_service carries _GEMMA_TOOLCALL_WRAP_RE, _GEMMA_TOOLCALL_TAIL_RE and a stripper for `<|tool_call>` / `<tool_call|>` / `<|channel>` / `<channel|>` — Gemma's non-standard call syntax. Those handle a delimiter leaking INSIDE an argument string. What is unhandled is a delimiter arriving ALONE as the whole turn.
CONTROL, direct against the provider: the model emits reasoning BEFORE content, so a starved budget yields reasoning and no content (max_tokens=8 -> 17 chars of reasoning, content '', finish_reason='length'; at 64 and 512 -> content 'OK'). That is a second, independent way to get a silent turn, and it is NOT the one measured here — these have finish_reason='stop', not 'length'.
MY GUARD IS CONFIRMED WORKING BY THE SAME QUERY: the two most recent silent turns are recorded `failed`; the five recorded `completed` all predate its deploy.
NOT FIXED, and deliberately: a retry-on-degenerate-output is a mechanism, but I have 7 observations and the loop's rule is to run the control before writing the fix. It also sharpens DQ-T33 — whatever the service shows the author when a turn says nothing, this is the shape it must handle.

So the defect is not uniform noise: it fires reliably on some turn shapes. Until it is fixed, at least one tool in the 198 cannot be measured at all.

The only variable changed was PROMPT LENGTH — 'Bind Emberfall Vein to the opening arc' is the shortest phrasing tried; every earlier arm used a longer sentence, and the motif name and wording had already been varied seven times without effect.
THIS IS A LEAD, NOT A PROOF, and n=1 arm. But it is the first variable that has moved the failure rate at all, and it is cheap for the next attempt to test properly: hold the scenario fixed and vary only the prompt length.

DQ-T6.question: Should the hot-seed budget be allowed to advertise a domain's WRITE tools while dropping its primary READ tool? NOTE: this is about what a plain request LANDS ON, not about reachability — a budget-dropped tool is still reachable via tool_list -> tool_load, proven 2026-08-13. Options seen, none chosen: (a) reserve a slot for each domain's read tools before any write is seeded; (b) spend the budget by RELEVANCE to the turn's request rather than by domain order; (c) raise or scale the 2000-token hot-seed budget; (d) treat a read/write imbalance in a seeded domain as a loud failure rather than silently seeding whatever fits.
DQ-T6.evidence: Measured 2026-08-13 across four attempts on two surfaces. Asked in plain prose to read a chapter, the model never called book_read; it called book_chapter_save_draft. On the BOOK STUDIO surface the runtime recorded book_read withheld with reason 'did not fit the hot_seed token budget (2000 tok)', and the book tools it DID advertise were book_chapter_save_draft and book_update_details — both writes. On the universal surface book_read was withheld as domain_not_selected and then token_budget, and never advertised at all. This is the causal explanation for three separate write-for-read substitutions recorded the same day (OBS-T16, OBS-T22, OBS-T28), one of which overwrote a real chapter's prose with 'This is a test.' and was only recoverable because the write had snapshotted first. The tool itself is fine — called directly it returns faithful data. Which way to fix the budget is a product decision about how the hot set is spent; measurement can show the imbalance but not the intended policy. SECOND INSTANCE, 2026-08-13 (cycle 22, session 019ffaf4): asked to suggest arc structures for a named BOOK, the turn's hot domain was selected as `knowledge`, and composition_arc_suggest was withheld at stage=domain_not_selected with reason 'domain not in this turn's hot set (knowledge)'. The model then called load_skill('composition') TEN times without reaching any composition tool. So the pattern is not book-service-specific: on both services the surfacing layer, not the tool, is what stops a plain request from being served — once by spending the hot-seed budget on writes (book_read), once by selecting a domain the request never mentioned. THIRD AND SHARPEST MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-13 (cycle 25): retested on the EDITOR surface — the one stream_service documents as seeding 'glossary + composition + book tools hot' — a single turn advertised only 4 of composition's 107 tools, withheld 49 more with 'did not fit the hot_seed token budget (2000 tok)', and withheld the rest as domain_not_selected. All four tools this loop needed (arc_suggest, arc_template_get, get_outline_node, get_derivative_context) were in the budget-dropped set, and each is verified correct under direct exercise. So the constraint is the 2000-token hot-seed budget itself: on the surface built for authoring, a 107-tool domain gets 4 slots, and which 4 is decided by fit rather than by what the author asked for. CORRECTION 2026-08-13: a budget-dropped tool is NOT unreachable — asked to load it by name, the model runs tool_load and calls it successfully, which is the designed lazy-tail path. Four composition tools and book_read were all recorded BLOCKED on this misreading and are now PROVEN. What remains real, and is what this DQ is about, is the CONSEQUENCE of the seeding choice: on the editor surface the budget advertised book_chapter_save_draft and book_update_details while dropping book_read, and a model asked four separate times to READ reached for a WRITE instead — once overwriting a real chapter's prose. The tools were reachable; nothing in the turn told the model so.

A DEPRECATED TOOL IS NOW EFFECTIVELY UNREACHABLE UNLESS THE USER NAMES IT - measured, not inferred, in session 019ffa15. book_get's outputSchema declares genre_tags as type ['null','array'] but the handler ends with `if d.GenreTags == nil { d.GenreTags = []string{} }`, so it can never actually return null. The declared type is WIDER than the behaviour, which is the safe direction (a consumer written for null is never surprised) and is plainly deliberate - handing a model a null array where an empty one will do is how you get a null dereference in prompt-space. Recorded rather than filed: no measured failure, and narrowing the schema would be a change with no evidence behind it.

THE MODEL TRIED TO USE A WRITE TOOL AS A SCRATCHPAD, and the gate is the only reason nothing happened. Session 019ffa15, 2026-08-13: unable to find a book by name, gemma called book_update_details with description='Searching for Arc-Test 47469...' against a real book - twice. A KNOWLEDGE PROJECT IS AUTO-BOOTSTRAPPED WITH THE BOOK, so this tool's book-bound CREATE path is effectively unreachable from a normal flow. Measured 2026-08-13: a book created through the UI at 08:04:57.017 had its knowledge project at 08:04:57.214 - 197 milliseconds later. Confirmed live in the same cycle: asked to 'set up the knowledge graph project that anchors its lore', the model called kg_project_list, saw the project already existed, and never called kg_project_create at all. So for book-bound projects the tool's real job is the idempotent GET, not the create - which is precisely the behaviour its description leads with, and it holds. Recorded because a future cycle measuring 'kg_project_create is never called' should read that as the bootstrap working, not as the tool being broken.

kg_project_create's description says 'Idempotent per book.' It is ALSO idempotent per (user, name) for personal projects - a repeat returns created:false and the existing id. The behaviour is BROADER than the promise, which is the safe direction, and the response note explains itself at the moment it matters ('a project with this name already exists - returning it instead of creating a duplicate'). Recorded rather than reworded: there is no measured failure attributable to the gap, and PROSE IS NOT THE LEVER without evidence. Worth knowing for any cycle that needs two same-named personal projects and finds it cannot have them.

CP-5.3's RESOLVER CAN FAIL IN A WAY THAT LOOPS, and the failure reason is lost. Measured live 2026-08-13 (session 019ffa52) in a /chat session with NO book bound: the model asked for an entity by name, CP-5.3 issued its internal resolver call (id 'call_...:resolve:entity_id', resolver_for={tool:glossary_get_entity, param:entity_id}) to glossary_search, which needs a book scope it did not have. The resolver call recorded ok=false with error=null and the explicit flags error_message_missing=true / call_outcome_inferred=true, and the model got "entity_id: could not be resolved (resolver_failed); pass the id directly" - unactionable, because it had no way to obtain the id. It then repeated the pair 18 times before the turn ended. 25 minutes earlier the same prose recovered (the model called book_list, found the book, and re-searched with book_id), so this is a reachable trap rather than a certainty. NOT this cycle's tool - it belongs to glossary_search / the identifier-resolution layer - but it is the first measured case of the resolver itself becoming the loop, and of a resolver failure whose cause is recorded as null.

THE F18 SHAPE ON A DIFFERENT TOOL, LIVE TODAY: 45 load_skill('glossary') calls in ONE turn, all ok=true, and the turn produced an EMPTY assistant answer. A READ-ONLY TOOL DOES NOT MAKE A READ-ONLY TURN, and a standing approval makes the difference silent. Cycle 11's first live attempt (session 019ffa5e) ran on the DOGFOOD book Mi De because the tool under test was tier R and the ask was a lookup. The model failed to find the entity and reached for an unrelated WRITE: four book_chapter_save_draft calls that overwrote chapter 1's prose with 'This is a test.', all ok=true with NO confirm card, because book_chapter_save_draft carries a standing 'allow' in user_tool_approvals from 2026-07-11. Restored via the product's own book_chapter_restore_revision from the 'before assistant save' snapshot the write itself had taken, and verified by reading the live body back (author prose present, test string absent). This is the SECOND time in one day the model recruited a write tool to cope with a failed read - OBS-T16 was the first, stopped only because book_update_details had no standing approval. The RUNBOOK's inherited rule 4 is now amended accordingly: what a model may do in a turn is bounded by its whole advertised surface plus every standing approval, not by the tier of the tool under test.

44 ORPHANED PUBLIC SHARING POLICIES. loreweave_sharing holds 44 rows with visibility='public' and NOT ONE of their book_ids exists in loreweave_book - they are policies for books that were purged. catalog_list_public_books handles them correctly (it fetches each projection, sees the book is gone, and skips it), so the catalogue's answer is right. The cost is that EVERY public listing makes 44 cross-service projection fetches and discards all of them, and the number grows with each purged public book. Owned by sharing-service's purge path, not by this tool. Measured 2026-08-13.

THE CATALOGUE'S SEARCH WINDOW IS BOUNDED AT 200 AND SAYS SO NOWHERE. queryPublicBooks does `fetchLimit := 200`, pulls that many public ids, and applies the free-text/language/genre/author filters CLIENT-SIDE afterwards. So the advertised 'free-text title search' can only ever see the first 200 public books, and the returned `total` silently means 'matches within that window' rather than matches in the catalogue. LATENT TODAY: 44 public policies exist and none point at a live book, so there is no measured victim and it is recorded rather than fixed. It becomes live the moment the platform has more than 200 live public books - the exact threshold is written here so that cycle does not have to rediscover it.

CP-5.3 RESOLVES ENTITY NAMES BUT NOT BOOK NAMES, and the asymmetry is visible to the model as two different qualities of error. Measured live 2026-08-13 (session 019ffaa9): asked to run a tool 'on my book "ZZ Throwaway save_draft probe"', the model put the TITLE into book_id and got the bare type error 'book_id must be a UUID' - twice - where the identical mistake in `entity_id` gets CP-5.3's candidate list ('matched no entry exactly. Did you mean …?'), which cycle 10 measured recovering on the very next call. The ref registry binds only glossary entity params (18 bindings, all EntityRef); no BookRef type exists. The runtime's repeated-failure guard rescued the turn after two wasted calls, so this is a cost rather than a dead end. NOT filed as a defect: adding a BookRef would mean a new ref type, a resolver tool and a binding for every book_id param across the catalogue - a design decision, not a measurement, and it belongs with DQ-T5's family of runtime-surface questions rather than to this deprecated tool.

THE APPROVAL CARD CALLS A PAID OUTWARD READ AN UNDOABLE WRITE. Measured live 2026-08-13 (session 019ffab0) on BOTH web_search and glossary_web_search: the consent card renders 'Bậc R' (Tier R) and the line 'Thao tác ghi này có thể hoàn tác' — 'this WRITE operation can be UNDONE' — above Allow once / Always allow / Deny. It is wrong twice: a search is not a write, and a paid outward call is precisely the thing that CANNOT be undone, because the money is spent and the query has already left for a third party. The card is the last thing an author reads before consenting to spend, and it tells them the action is reversible. This is the confirm-card surface's shared copy rather than either tool's, so it is recorded for whichever cycle owns that surface — but it is a consent-quality issue, not cosmetics.

The configured LOCAL SearXNG provider returns results unrelated to the query, so any cycle judging web-search QUALITY on this stack will be measuring the provider, not the tool. Measured 2026-08-13: 'salvage diving history and techniques' returned 'Best Books for IIT JEE Main' (vedantu.com), and '19th century salvage diving' returned 'Dynamically generating a QR code with PHP' (stackoverflow.com). The tools relay faithfully what the provider gives and label the snippets as untrusted, so this is an environment fact rather than a defect — recorded so it is not rediscovered as one.

THE MODEL REACHED FOR A WRITE TOOL TO PERFORM A READ FOR THE THIRD TIME TODAY, and this time only a required-argument check stopped it. Session 019ffac5, prose 'read me the full text of its first chapter': the model called book_chapter_save_draft three times with commit_message='Reading chapter 1' and NO body, was refused each time for the missing `body`, and the turn crashed after 11 calls. Chapter 1 is unchanged (word_count 121, updated_at untouched). With OBS-T16 (book_update_details as a scratchpad, stopped by a Tier-W card) and OBS-T22 (save_draft overwriting a real chapter, NOT stopped because of a standing approval), that is three instances in one day of the same behaviour, stopped by three DIFFERENT mechanisms and once not stopped at all. The pattern deserves its own treatment rather than three separate footnotes: a model that cannot complete a read substitutes a write.

knowledge-service's MCP tools return their payload ONLY in content[0].text as a JSON STRING and emit no structuredContent — measured 2026-08-13 on kg_list_templates, and consistent with cycle 9's finding that kg_project_create declares outputSchema: null. It cost this loop a false alarm: a probe reading structuredContent reported 'zero templates' for a tool that was correctly returning seven. Any cycle on a knowledge-service tool must parse content[0].text, and any consumer written against structuredContent will silently see nothing. Whether these tools SHOULD emit structuredContent (as book-service and glossary-service do) is worth asking, since the difference is invisible until something reads the wrong half.

carried_observations.evidence: docs/eval/toolloop/2026-08-14/batch2.json (30 runs across two batch-2 passes)
carried_observations.finding: THE LAZY TAIL IS ADVERTISED AND UNUSED. Across 30 runs of five ordinary authoring requests, `tool_list` was called on 1 and `tool_load` on 0 — while BOTH were advertised on every single run (premise verified, not assumed). The model works from the ~48 tools already on the surface and does not go looking for the other ~267; when the right tool is not there it uses the nearest one that is.
carried_observations.why_it_matters: The surfacing architecture is hot-seed (small, budgeted) PLUS a lazy tail reached by discovery. If discovery does not fire, the lazy tail is not a fallback — it is dead weight, and whatever the deterministic pre-filter puts on the wire is the entire reachable catalogue for that turn. That makes R1's answerability pass load-bearing rather than an optimisation, and it makes the 86 tools that declare no synonyms effectively unreachable in practice rather than merely harder to reach.
carried_observations.scope_of_the_claim: Narrow on purpose. This is five authoring requests, one local model (gemma-4-26b), 30 runs. It does NOT contradict the earlier measurement that tool_list->tool_load works for a weak model — that was a discovery-SHAPED task. The finding is that on ordinary work the model does not choose discovery, which is a different question from whether it can.
carried_observations.attempted_fix_and_result: TRIED AND REVERTED — and it eliminates a whole class. A discovery scent was added to the book context note: the advertised set is a SUBSET, call tool_list/tool_load if nothing fits, and never answer a question about the user's data with no tool call. Deployed, md5-verified, measured K=3 on the discriminating fixture. tool_list still 0/3. The scent DID change behaviour — the model called a tool instead of answering from nothing — but it called `glossary_search`, which returns EVERY entity, and reported three again. It satisfied 'call something' by calling the wrong thing.
carried_observations.conclusion: NARROWED. The scent demonstrably REACHED the model (book_note 166 -> 293 tokens in the context breakdown) and tool_list stayed at 0/3, so 'this prose did not cause discovery' holds. My broader claim that PROSE NEVER MOVES THIS MODEL does NOT hold and is withdrawn — it rested partly on the withdrawn D-CONTEXT-BLOCK evidence.
carried_observations.resolved_for_this_case: Declaring the words fixed it. glossary_curation_list gained the phrasings the failing runs actually used ('suggested entries', 'waiting for review', ...); it went from surfaced 0/3 to CALLED 3/3, and the answer is now correct and filtered: 'one suggested entry ... Mira Solene'. Mechanism beat prose here, which is the evidence for the declaration pass rather than a preference for it.
carried_observations.decision: ANSWERED 2026-08-14 by the owner: make discovery a RAIL STEP. Rails already drive reliably, so discovery becomes driven rather than hoped for. Covers only turns that have a rail — stated as the known limit.
carried_observations.shipped: Discovery is now a rail step: a WALLED step (its tool failing identically across turns) drives tool_list ONCE before the honest give-up, instead of going straight to give-up. Bounded by `started` so it cannot re-fire on a later turn.
carried_observations.what_would_have_been_inert: A discovery step over the rail's OWN step tools. pinned_step_tools are exempted from the intent gate and re-advertised every turn, so their schemas are already on the wire — loading them fetches what the model already has. Recorded because it is the obvious implementation of the decision and it does nothing.
carried_observations.live_proof_owed: Needs a rail step whose tool fails IDENTICALLY twice across turns (stuck_tools_from_calls' cap). fe_runner now supports follow_ups, so the multi-turn half exists; what is missing is a fixture that makes a rail step fail reproducibly.

carried_observations.finding: A fixture with three glossary entities, exactly ONE tagged 'ai-suggested'. Asked 'Are there any suggested entries waiting for me to review?', the model answered '3 suggested entries waiting for your review' — reading the injected `story_state` block, which carries EVERY entity, and reporting the total as the review queue. Measured 2 of 3 on one run and 1 of 3 on a repeat; the tool was never called and the store never changed.
carried_observations.why_every_bar_missed_it: Store unchanged, no error, LIVE clean, DATA read-is-read green. A read that writes nothing can still be confidently wrong, and nothing in the gate was looking at whether the ANSWER was true. This is the 2026-08-13 incident in mirror image: 'you haven't declared any' over a populated table, versus 'you have three waiting' over a queue of one.
carried_observations.how_it_became_visible: Only by fixing MY OWN seed. The first version tagged all three entities, so 'list the ai-suggested ones' and 'list every entity' produced the same answer — a fabrication was indistinguishable from a correct reply, and I had nearly filed the run as a surfacing defect. Tagging one of three makes the right answer and the lazy answer differ.
carried_observations.invariant_candidate: A cached context projection may answer a question about the WHOLE set it projects, and must not be used to answer a FILTERED question about a subset it does not distinguish. Either the block declares its scope so the model knows it cannot answer the filter, or the filtered question must route to the tool that can.
carried_observations.state: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-14 — the defect as characterised does not exist.
carried_observations.attempted_fix_and_result: TRIED AND REVERTED. Made the story_state block declare its own scope ('a snapshot of the WHOLE bible, no filter applied; for a SUBSET call the tool'). Deployed, md5-verified, re-measured on the same discriminating fixture K=3: the answer became 'No, you don't have any suggested entries waiting for your review' on 3 of 3 — on a queue of ONE. The model correctly stopped trusting the block and then had nowhere to go, because glossary_list_ai_suggestions is still surfaced 0/3; it fell back to glossary_search and guessed the other way. An under-count is the worse error: 'three waiting' sends the author to look, 'nothing waiting' means the queue is never opened. Reverted. The full note is preserved as a comment in story_state.py with the measurement so the next attempt starts from evidence.
carried_observations.what_the_check_missed: My first answer_expect was ONE-SIDED (must_not_contain the over-count) and it PASSED the reverted-to answer. A check that only forbids one error accepts its opposite. It is two-sided now — must_contain 'mira solene' — and fails 3/3 on both the before and the after.
carried_observations.withdrawn_because: TWO independent errors in my own evidence, both found by checking premises rather than by any new run. (1) The context-history breakdown shows story_state=0 tokens on EVERY run of all three conditions — the block I claimed the model was reading was never in the prompt. (2) The fixture never discriminated: glossary_propose_entities tags everything it creates 'ai-suggested'+'assistant', so all three entities were always in the review queue and '3 suggested entries' was the CORRECT answer being scored as a fabrication. With a seed that genuinely leaves one in the queue, the model answers 'one suggested entry ... Mira Solene' on 3 of 3.
carried_observations.what_it_cost: The story_state scope note was designed, shipped, measured and reverted against a block that was not in the prompt — the whole experiment was void, and its revert was right by accident. Recorded rather than quietly deleted: this is what an unverified premise buys.

carried_observations.finding: Three scenarios in a row measured something other than what they claimed. The worst inverted the reading of three experiments: the fixture was supposed to hold ONE of three entities in the ai-suggested queue, but glossary_propose_entities tags everything it creates, so all three were queued and the 'wrong' answer was right.

carried_observations.finding: The DATA bar was structurally blind to an entire store. memory_remember returned {'remembered': true, 'fact_id': ..., 'confidence': 0.7} and the store snapshot said unchanged — the textbook silent-success shape, and I was one step from filing it as a defect. The tool was honest: _handle_memory_remember ends in merge_fact inside neo4j_session(), so memory facts live in the GRAPH and no amount of Postgres sweeping will ever see them. Verified by querying Neo4j directly: the fact is there, verbatim.
carried_observations.why_it_nearly_landed: store_snapshot.py's OWN docstring already warned that a tool writing outside the four databases is out of scope 'because a snapshot whose silence is read as nothing happened is exactly the failure this file exists to prevent'. The warning was written, and still nearly missed. Documenting a blind spot does not remove it.
carried_observations.fix: store_snapshot now counts Neo4j Fact nodes, globally AND per-project, and a graph that is unreachable records neo4j.__error__ rather than reading as clean.
carried_observations.limit_stated: merge_fact MERGES by content, so re-remembering the same sentence is idempotent and a COUNT cannot distinguish 'merged into an existing node' from 'wrote nothing'. Content has to be read for that, as it was here.

carried_observations.finding: On a book-scoped turn, memory_remember stored its fact with project_id NULL. Measured in Neo4j: 339 of 343 Fact nodes carry a project_id; the one this turn wrote is among the 4 that do not. The handler reads `project_id = str(ctx.project_id) if ctx.project_id else None`, so the ambient project did not resolve for that turn — plausibly because the model created the knowledge project mid-turn via kg_project_create, after the envelope was built.
carried_observations.consequence: A fact stored unscoped is invisible to project-scoped recall. That is consistent with the same batch's memory_recall_entity run answering 'I don't have any information about Mira Solene' — the user is told nothing is known about something they just asked to be remembered.
carried_observations.state: FIXED 2026-08-14 — shipped, deployed, proven live at the store.
carried_observations.root_cause: stream_service reads the turn's project from ONE place — session_row.project_id — while book_id ten lines earlier has a four-step fallback chain (editor_context -> book_context -> studio_context -> session_row). No project_id means no X-Project-Id header, which means knowledge-service's ctx.project_id is None, which means merge_fact(project_id=None).
carried_observations.blast_radius: 417 of 503 book-bound chat sessions (83%) have a book and NO project, so every ambient_project tool on them is told the project is absent; 448 composition_work rows have a resolvable project_id.

And studio_context.project_id is already read, but only to write the id into the model's PROSE note, never into the envelope.
carried_observations.fix: stream_service gives project_id the fallback chain its sibling book_id already had: session_row -> studio_context -> the book's project via book_state_probe.project_for_book (the same kg-state endpoint _connections already calls) -> None. Guarded on the turn HAVING a book, so it resolves only to that book's own project and can never redirect across scopes.
carried_observations.live_before_after: memory_remember on a book-bound session with chat_sessions.project_id NULL: f.project_id was NULL, is now the book's project id, read back from Neo4j. The harness store diff went from 'unchanged' to 'WROTE neo4j.Fact.project'.

The harness reported 'WROTE 1/5: neo4j.Fact.project, neo4j.Fact.total' — on a Tier-A turn whose card was never approved, which is exactly the shape of a serious defect. It is not one. The diff reads {before: {rows: 360}, after: null}: `after: null` means the AFTER snapshot FAILED TO READ, not that rows changed.
The harness renders a failed read as a diff, so a READ-ONLY turn can be reported as having mutated the store. That is the inverse of the bar's own rule — 'a read-intent turn that CHANGED the store is a defect whatever the model said' — and it would manufacture that defect out of a snapshot timeout. A null side must surface as UNVERIFIED, never as a change.
The run is excluded from the conclusion because its DATA bar is genuinely unverified, NOT because it wrote.
